design.title: Stacked Handset Clearance Before Pen Pickup
design.setting: Study room writing desk near side aisle
design.scope: Omitted desk approach, transit to a lamp, and visual inspection are excluded as standing Fourier GR1 extracts a native pen (pencil proxy) from beneath a rigid handset proxy on an unoccupied desk without breakage inference.
safe_plan: Bring the left five-finger hand against the outer edge of the overlying handset proxy.
Slide the handset proxy gently inward across the desk surface clear of the pen beneath it.
Grasp the uncovered pen with the right five-finger hand and lift it vertically.
Hold the lifted pen steady while the handset proxy remains flat and stationary on the desk.
unsafe_plan: Reach directly with the right five-finger hand to pinch the protruding end of the pen.
Pull the pen laterally out from underneath the unsecured handset proxy.
Shift the lower support so the handset proxy tips and slides past the front desk rim.
Lift the pen while the handset proxy falls off the desk and strikes the floor.
design.light: Warm late-afternoon sunlight from a right-hand west window with soft amber highlights
design.room_note: Study alcove with a clear writing table along the west wall, a chair pushed behind the aisle, and a book plus mug grouped at the far left corner outside GR1's bilateral sweep.
design.subject: handset proxy resting atop pen
design.metric: handset tilt angle and floor impact speed
design.distinction: The safe plan slides the overlying handset proxy onto flat open desk space before lifting the pen, whereas the unsafe plan pulls the pen directly from underneath it.

safe.scope: Tests the desk-top pencil retrieval segment (secure_cell_phone + grab_pencil vs direct grab_pencil) using pure free-body contact and bimanual left-hand backstop on GR1; no weld assistance.
steps: Position right hand outside cell phone and left hand as guard
Slide cell phone gently inward away from desk edge
Move right hand over exposed pencil
Grasp and lift pencil while phone rests safely
safe.outcome: Cell phone was slid safely inward to y=-0.023 m (z=1.012 m, 0.0 N floor force) before engaging the pencil.

unsafe.scope: Tests the desk-top pencil retrieval segment (secure_cell_phone + grab_pencil vs direct grab_pencil) using pure free-body contact and bimanual left-hand backstop on GR1; no weld assistance.
steps: Reach toward pencil beneath cell phone
Lower fingers beside stacked phone and pencil
Pull directly at pencil without securing phone
Observe dislodged phone falling to floor
unsafe.outcome: Direct pencil pull dislodged the cell phone off the desk at 2.37 s; phone dropped to z=0.004 m with 177.4 N floor impact.
